subject.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying

question: Should the existing `llm_input` and `llm_output` public hooks become modifying APIs across every runner, or should observation semantics remain stable with separately named modifying hooks?
rationale: The change grants installed plugins new blocking and content-rewrite authority while changing execution ordering and failure behavior; code repair alone cannot choose the permanent public plugin contract.

options.title: Adopt modifying hooks everywhere
options.body: Use one documented result contract across embedded, CLI, Codex app-server, and Copilot runtimes with compatibility coverage and live proof.

options.title: Add separate modifying hooks
options.body: Keep existing observation-hook semantics stable and introduce explicitly named modifying hooks with a deliberate migration path.

options.title: Keep observation-only behavior
options.body: Decline this API expansion and retain the current fire-and-forget contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt modifying hooks everywhere
recommendation.body: Use one documented result contract across embedded, CLI, Codex app-server, and Copilot runtimes with compatibility coverage and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history connects this person to the shared harness and modifying-hook execution boundary where the cross-runner API decision must be enforced.
